title: Glossary
markdown:
Every term from the course, in alphabetical order. The lesson that introduces each one is in brackets.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Abstract class** | A TypeScript class that cannot be created with `new`; it shares code and declares methods subclasses must write. (5.05) |
| **AbortController** | An object whose `signal` cancels a `fetch` or other operation when `abort()` is called. (4.04) |
| **Action** | A plain object describing what happened, such as `{ type: "add", name: "Read" }`, handled by an update function. (6.05) |
| **any** | The TypeScript type that switches checking off for a value. Avoid it. (5.01) |
| **Arrow function** | A short function form: `x => x * 2`. It has no `this` of its own. (2.01) |
| **async function** | A function that always returns a promise and may use `await` inside. (4.03) |
| **await** | Pauses an async function until a promise settles, then gives its value or throws its error. (4.03) |
| **Bubbling** | An event running listeners on its target, then on each parent up to the document. (6.02) |
| **Bundler** | A tool, such as Vite, that serves files during development and combines and optimises them for production. (6.04) |
| **Call stack** | The functions running right now, each waiting for the one above it. (4.01) |
| **Callback** | A function passed to another function, to be called later. (2.01) |
| **Class** | A description of a kind of object: its fields, constructor and methods. (3.01) |
| **Closure** | A function together with the variables of the scope it was created in, which it keeps using. (2.04) |
| **CommonJS** | Node's older module system, with `require` and `module.exports`. (3.05) |
| **Concurrency limit** | Running at most N asynchronous tasks at the same time, for example with a worker pool. (4.05) |
| **const** | Declares a variable that cannot be reassigned (its object can still change). (1.02) |
| **CORS** | The browser rule that a page may read responses from another site only if that site allows it. (4.04) |
| **Debounce** | Running a function once the calls to it have stopped for a while. (4.05) |
| **Default export** | The one unnamed export of a module, imported without braces. (3.05) |
| **Destructuring** | Taking values out of objects and arrays into variables: `const { name } = user`. (2.03) |
| **devDependency** | A package needed only while developing or building, such as a test runner. (6.04) |
| **Discriminated union** | A union whose variants share a tag property with different literal types, such as `kind`. (5.03) |
| **DOM** | The tree of objects a browser builds from HTML, which JavaScript reads and changes. (6.01) |
| **Enum** | A TypeScript set of named constants that also exists at run time. (5.05) |
| **Error-first callback** | Node's callback style: `(err, value) => ...`, with `err` null on success. (4.01) |
| **ES module** | A file with its own scope that shares values with `export` and `import`. (3.05) |
| **Event delegation** | Handling events of many child elements with one listener on a parent. (6.02) |
| **Event loop** | The mechanism that runs queued tasks and microtasks one at a time when the call stack is empty. (4.01) |
| **Exhaustive check** | Assigning to `never` in a switch's default, so that unhandled variants fail to compile. (5.03) |
| **fetch** | The function that makes HTTP requests and returns a promise for a Response. (4.04) |
| **FormData** | An object collecting a form's named fields; all values are strings. (6.02) |
| **Generator** | A `function*` that produces values one at a time with `yield`, pausing between them. (3.04) |
| **Generic** | A function, interface or class with a type parameter, such as `first<T>(items: T[]): T`. (5.04) |
| **Getter / setter** | Methods that run when a property is read (`get`) or assigned (`set`). (3.01) |
| **Hoisting** | Function declarations being usable before the line that defines them. (2.01) |
| **Immutability** | Not changing existing values; building new ones instead, as `update` does. (6.05) |
| **Inference** | TypeScript working out a type from a value, so it need not be written. (5.01) |
| **Interface** | A named description of an object's shape. (5.02) |
| **Iterable** | An object with a `[Symbol.iterator]()` method, usable in `for...of` and spread. (3.04) |
| **JSON** | The text format for data, written like JavaScript literals with double-quoted keys. (2.05) |
| **keyof** | The union of a type's property names. (5.04) |
| **let** | Declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned. (1.02) |
| **Literal type** | A type allowing one exact value, such as `"up"` or `3`. (5.03) |
| **Lock file** | `package-lock.json`: the exact version of every installed package. (6.04) |
| **localStorage** | Per-site string storage in the browser that survives reloads. (6.03) |
| **Map** | A collection of key-value pairs with keys of any type, in insertion order. (2.05) |
| **Microtask** | A callback, such as a promise reaction, that runs as soon as the current code finishes, before the next task. (4.01) |
| **Migration** | Converting stored data from an older version's shape to the current one. (6.03) |
| **Narrowing** | TypeScript working out a more exact type after a check such as `typeof x === "string"`. (5.03) |
| **never** | The type with no values: code that cannot be reached. (5.03) |
| **npm** | Node's package manager, which installs packages and runs scripts from `package.json`. (6.04) |
| **Nullish** | `null` or `undefined`, the values that `??` and `?.` look for. (1.03) |
| **Optional chaining** | `a?.b`: stops and gives `undefined` when `a` is null or undefined. (1.03) |
| **Parameter property** | A TypeScript constructor parameter with `public`, `private` or `readonly` that also declares the property. (5.05) |
| **Polymorphism** | Different classes answering the same method call in their own way. (3.01) |
| **Private field** | A class field whose name starts with `#`, reachable only inside the class. (3.01) |
| **Promise** | An object standing for a result that arrives later: pending, then fulfilled or rejected. (4.02) |
| **Prototype** | The object another object falls back to for properties it does not have itself. (3.02) |
| **Pure function** | A function whose result depends only on its arguments and that changes nothing outside itself. (2.01) |
| **Rest parameter** | `...args` in a function definition: collects the remaining arguments into an array. (2.01) |
| **Scope** | The region of code where a variable can be used. (2.04) |
| **Semantic versioning** | `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` version numbers, where a major change may break code. (6.04) |
| **Set** | A collection of unique values. (2.05) |
| **Spread** | `...x` in a call, array or object literal: expands its items or properties. (2.01) |
| **State** | The data that describes everything an app shows; the page is rendered from it. (6.01) |
| **Strict equality** | `===`: equal without type conversion. (1.03) |
| **Structural typing** | TypeScript comparing types by their shape rather than their name. (5.02) |
| **Template literal** | A string in backticks that can contain `${expressions}` and line breaks. (1.04) |
| **this** | The object a function was called on, decided at call time. (3.02) |
| **Throttle** | Running a function at most once per period. (4.05) |
| **Truthy / falsy** | How a value counts in a condition; the falsy values are `false`, `0`, `""`, `null`, `undefined` and `NaN`. (1.02) |
| **Tuple** | A TypeScript array type with a fixed length and a type per position: `[string, number]`. (5.01) |
| **Type alias** | A name for any type: `type Id = string \| number`. (5.02) |
| **Type assertion** | `value as Type`: telling the compiler to treat a value as a type without checking. (5.03) |
| **Type guard** | A function returning `x is T`, which narrows its argument when it returns true. (5.03) |
| **TypeScript** | JavaScript with type annotations, checked by a compiler and then removed. (5.01) |
| **typeof** | The operator giving a value's type as a string, such as `"number"`. (1.02) |
| **Union type** | `A \| B`: a value that is one of several types. (5.03) |
| **unknown** | The TypeScript type for any value that must be checked before use. (5.01) |
| **Utility type** | A built-in generic that transforms a type: `Partial`, `Pick`, `Omit`, `Record`. (5.05) |
| **XSS** | Cross-site scripting: injected HTML or script running in a page, often through `innerHTML`. (6.01) |
